summary: Chrome service-worker rebuffering after long tab pause causes SSE event boundary corruption and interleaved choices
description:
Issue summary:
Customer observed SSE streams from the Redwood API delivering garbled final choices after resuming a paused browser tab. The stream plays correctly initially; after leaving the tab backgrounded for ~20–30s and then returning, the final choice is split across fragments and then interleaved with a subsequent choice. This results in malformed structured output for the application and a user-visible truncated sentence.

Impact:
- Multiple end users at Streamly.ai report corrupted assistant responses in production for ~6% of resumed streams in us-west-2.
- Breaks downstream parsers that expect well-formed JSON or terminal choice markers.

Environment:
- Client: Chrome 106 on macOS Monterey and Chrome 106 on Linux. Also seen in Chrome-based embedded webview.
- Customer uses a client-side service worker which intercepts fetch events and applies range/rebuffering logic to improve battery/latency for background tabs.
- Redwood API model: redwood-v1-medium (pinned) via hosted endpoint behind Cloudflare + internal edge proxy.

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer and reproduced by support):
1) Start streaming completion via SSE from UI in foreground tab (payload includes structured choices and "end" marker).
2) Let the stream run for ~2–3s, then background the tab (put to sleep) for ~20–40s.
3) The client service worker intercepts revalidation and issues range-style re-requests for the stream upon resume.
4) On tab resume, the browser/service-worker pipeline coalesces/reattributes incoming bytes and we observe out-of-order chunk delivery and partial event merges.
5) Client parses resulting SSE stream and fails to reconstruct final choice boundaries; final sentence fragments are split and interleaved with next-choice tokens.

Relevant request ids / logs (customer supplied):
- customer request-id: streamly-req-20260308-77a1
- edge request-id: rwd-edge-0a9f2b03
- approximate time: 2026-03-08T21:14:03Z

Initial investigation notes:
- Reproduced locally with Chrome 106 when using a synthetic service worker that rewrites range bytes and replays portions of the stream on resume.
- Observed that when Service Worker fetch handler returns a ReadableStream that performs byte-slicing and concatenation, the browser's framing of text/event-stream boundaries can be altered (Content-Type unchanged).
- Edge logs show no 5xx; connection remained open and returned 200 with transfer-encoding: chunked. No server-side errors recorded.
- Hypothesis: client-side rebuffering/replay by service worker changes the chunk boundary alignment; SSE event parsing in the browser then groups bytes differently leading to event frames that contain partial choices or multiple events merged.

Temporary workarounds suggested to customer:
- Disable service worker interception for streaming endpoints (simplest) or return a passthrough response for any URL matching /v1/stream/* to avoid client-side range reassembly.
- Use WebSocket fallback rather than SSE for clients that require aggressive SW caching.
- Shorten background pause deadline (keepalive pings) so the browser does not trigger service worker byte slicing on resume.

Engineering next steps / proposed fixes:
- Add guidance to SDK docs to set Cache-Control: no-transform and to avoid service-worker reassembly for streaming endpoints.
- Server-side: add an SSE-safe chunk boundary marker (internal event boundary) that clients can use to validate event framing when resuming. This requires a small runtime change to emit explicit end-of-choice markers on their own line.
- Intake a task to detect abnormal resume offsets and return 409/+Retry-After to force clients to reopen a fresh stream when we detect non-sequential byte offsets (P2 engineering ticket to spec).

Attachments provided by customer: sample HAR with SW handling, a client-side service worker snippet, and a screen recording of resumed stream showing interleaved tokens.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer report received. Reproduced in-house with SW snippet. Escalating to serving-runtime for hypothesis validation.
2026-03-11 - Diego Alvarez (Serving Runtime): Confirmed chunk coalescing behavior on resume path. Will instrument runtime to emit per-chunk indices and correlation id for next 48h for reruns.

2026-03-12 - Elena Park (SRE): Edge proxy logs indicate no resets; Cloudflare did not mutate chunking but our internal edge may coalesce small writes. Adding an experimental header x-sse-chunk-id to pass through for repro runs.
2026-03-13 - Streamly.ai (Customer): Implemented workaround to bypass SW for streams and confirmed immediate drop of corrupted resumes. Customer requests ETA for server-side marker fix.

2026-03-14 - Diego Alvarez (Serving Runtime): Proposal drafted: emit explicit \"event: choice-boundary\" marker after each completed choice and publish SDK guidance. Planning PR for next minor release (target 2026-03-21).
resolution: Workaround accepted by customer (disable SW for streaming endpoints). Engineering to ship explicit SSE choice-boundary markers in serving runtime; PR planned for 2026-03-21. Follow-up tasks: create internal ticket to detect non-sequential resume offsets and update docs.
notes: This ticket is high priority because it affects structured-output integrations. Related to prior proxy/utf8 boundary tickets but root cause here is client-side SW rebuffering in Chrome; coordinated mitigation will be both docs and runtime marker emission.
